# dsh-reader implementation contracts

This file is the interface contract between the reader shell (owned by the Lead),
the PDF engine, and the document-format engine. Keep these shapes stable unless the
Lead updates this file first.

## Owned paths (do not edit another owner's paths)

| Owner | Paths |
| --- | --- |
| Lead | `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `lib/**`, `web/src/index.jsx`, `web/src/app.jsx`, `web/src/components/**`, `web/src/styles.js`, `web/src/storage.js`, `web/src/ai-client.js`, `scripts/build-client.mjs`, `scripts/copy-assets.mjs`, `client/**`, `README*` |
| PDF engine | `web/src/pdf/**`, `scripts/build-pdf.mjs`, `tests/pdf-*`, `test/fixtures/pdf-*` |
| Format engine | `web/src/formats/**`, `tests/formats-*`, `test/fixtures/formats-*` |

`dist/**` is generated by the build scripts; never hand-edit it.

## Normalized book shape (format engine)

```js
/**
 * @typedef {Object} NormalizedBook
 * @property {'epub'|'mobi'|'txt'|'md'|'html'} format
 * @property {string} title
 * @property {string} [author]
 * @property {string} [language]       // BCP-47-ish, best effort
 * @property {Chapter[]} chapters
 * @property {TocEntry[]} toc
 * @property {string[]} warnings
 * @property {() => void} [dispose]    // revoke any object URLs created by the parser
 */

/**
 * @typedef {Object} Chapter
 * @property {string} id
 * @property {string} title
 * @property {Block[]} blocks
 */

/**
 * @typedef {Object} Block
 * @property {string} id             // unique inside the book
 * @property {'heading'|'paragraph'|'list-item'|'quote'|'image'|'table'|'code'|'rule'} kind
 * @property {string} [html]         // sanitized inline HTML, for heading/paragraph/list-item/quote/table/code
 * @property {string} [text]         // plain text of `html`, used by translation and AI
 * @property {number} [level]        // heading level 1..6
 * @property {string} [src]          // object URL for an image block
 * @property {string} [alt]
 * @property {string} [caption]
 */

/**
 * @typedef {Object} TocEntry
 * @property {string} title
 * @property {number} chapterIndex  // 0-based
 * @property {number} [depth]
 */
```

Required export from `web/src/formats/index.js`:

```js
export async function parseBook(blob, { fileName, mime } = {}) : Promise<NormalizedBook>
export function extensionOf(fileName) : string  // lowercase, no dot
```

Rules:

- Never execute scripts from documents. Sanitize document HTML before it reaches `html`.
- Inline markup allowed in `html`: `b, strong, i, em, u, s, sub, sup, code, span, a, br, ruby, rt, rp, small, mark`.
  Strip every attribute except `href` on `a`; resolve EPUB internal links to `data-chapter` + `data-anchor`
  or leave a safe `href` for external links.
- Image blocks carry a browser object URL in `src`; collect all created URLs and revoke them in `dispose()`.
- TXT decoding: BOM-aware UTF-8/UTF-16, then UTF-8 fatal, then GB18030. Split chapters on Chinese
  `第…章/节/回` and English `Chapter N` headings; if none, one chapter.
- EPUB: parse `META-INF/container.xml` → OPF → manifest/spine/nav (EPUB3) or NCX; include cover metadata when cheap.
  Preserve reading order. Use `fflate` (`unzipSync`) and `DOMPurify` (browser `window`).
- MOBI: prefer `@lingo-reader/mobi-parser` if it works in the bundle; otherwise implement a minimal
  PalmDOC/MOBI reader (uncompressed + PalmDOC LZ77 are mandatory; HUFF/CDIC optional with a clear warning).
  Return a useful error for DRM-protected or unsupported books.
- `parseBook` must reject with `Error` carrying a human-readable Chinese `message` on unsupported/corrupt input.
- Keep the package browser-only; no Node built-ins.

## PDF engine shape

`web/src/pdf/PdfViewer.jsx` default-exports a React component. It may import React
(`import React from 'react'`; the client build externalizes `react`).

Props:

```js
{
  data: Uint8Array | Blob,          // bytes are not mutated; Blob avoids a full UI-thread copy
  documentId?: string,             // library id enables managed, cached sidebar translation
  fileName: string,
  initialPage?: number,             // 1-based, restore progress
  autoTranslate?: boolean,
  pageTranslations?: {              // keyed by page number (1-based)
    [page: number]: {
      status: 'loading'|'done'|'error',
      segments?: { src: string, zh: string }[],
      error?: string,
    }
  },
  onReady?: ({ pageCount: number }) => void,
  onPageChange?: (page: number) => void,
  onPageText?: (page: number, payload: { text: string, segments: { src: string }[] }) => void,
  onSelection?: (sel: {
    text: string,
    page: number,
    rect: DOMRect,
    context?: string,
  } | null) => void,
  onRetryTranslation?: (page: number) => void,
  onHideTranslations?: () => void,
}
```

It must:

- Dynamically `import('/dsh-reader-assets/pdf.bundle.js')` so the startup client bundle stays light.
- Use `pdf/engine.js` to set version-matched parsing `workerSrc` and drawing
  `rendererSrc`; ship both worker assets. Verify the parser is a real Worker.
- Render continuous pages at fit-width with lazy canvas rendering, text layer spans that support native
  selection, page gap/placeholder, keyboard PageUp/PageDown/Home/End, and a compact own toolbar
  (zoom, fit width, page input, previous/next).
- Extract per-page paragraph segments (`{ src }`) for translation, call `onPageText` once per page
  when it first becomes visible (only if `autoTranslate` is true), and show `pageTranslations`
  in an independently scrolling “中文对照” pane. Translation updates must not
  add height to the PDF pages. For a supplied documentId, the viewer owns the
  paragraph translation controller and persistent cache; onPageText remains an
  optional visible-page notification. Hosts without documentId may still supply
  pageTranslations/onRetryTranslation externally.
- Call `onSelection` on mouseup/keyup with the selected text and bounding rect, and `onSelection(null)`
  when the selection collapses. Include nearby page text as `context` (bounded ~600 chars).
- Apply `data-ds-dark-theme` / `prefers-color-scheme` friendly colors; export `pdfStyles` CSS string
  from the module so the shell can inject it once.
- Never import `pdfjs-dist` statically from `PdfViewer.jsx`; only the lazy module may do that.

Also export:

```js
export const pdfStyles: string
export function groupPdfText(items): { text: string, segments: { src: string }[] }
```

`groupPdfText` is pure and should have a Node test with fabricated `getTextContent` items.

The PDF parsing/rendering workers and cMaps are built/copied into `dist/reader-assets/` by `scripts/build-pdf.mjs`
and served by the Host at `/dsh-reader-assets/`.

## Horizontal navigation invariants

- Flow formats share `components/flow-pagination.js` and one explicit cursor per
  reader instance. Scroll events and animation completion must never infer a
  different book page or mutate its breakpoints.
- Measure text only after presentation transforms have been removed. Layout
  changes preserve a character anchor; oversized objects and the final page
  must remain reachable.
- Initial restore and annotation navigation use the cancelable
  `dshr-flow-navigate` event on the scroll element. Later user navigation
  invalidates delayed work. Cancel all old animation/layout work on chapter or
  document replacement.
- PDF keeps its own explicit page state. Common controls forward
  `dshr-pdf-page-turn` and mirror `dshr-pdf-page-state`, without inferring PDF
  pages from scroll offsets.
- Validate shared navigation changes with unit tests and both
  `npm run test:flow-browser` and `npm run test:pdf-browser`.

## PDF sidebar translation invariants

- Text item indices and stable paragraph ids link PDF.js text spans to sidebar
  cards. Original canvas, native selection and annotation geometry remain owned
  by PdfViewer. Sidebar selection must not create annotations on the original.
- TranslationController has at most two active jobs, prioritizes visible
  paragraphs/current page, and starts optional next-page work only after current
  work settles. A bounded client timeout releases jobs even if transport stalls.
- Abort and epoch checks isolate navigation, pause, document, glossary and model
  changes. The Host forwards cancellation to the LLM and rejects stale model
  identities before starting generation.
- Cache keys include document id, paragraph text, target language, model/provider,
  glossary, and client/server prompt versions. Cache errors cannot block reading.
  Database v3 adds pdfTranslations without dropping the v2 book/annotation/assets
  stores; deleting a book also removes its cached translations/preferences.
- Completed text remains readable while manually retranslating; retry affects
  only the selected/failed paragraphs. Formula/reference placeholders must be
  restored exactly or the paragraph is marked failed instead of silently damaged.
- Side-pane wheel/keyboard/scroll and async results must never turn the PDF page.
  Controls are positioned over the original viewport, including narrow layouts.
- Validate changes with `npm run test:translation-browser`, which uses a local
  deterministic fake translator rather than a paid model.

## PDF performance invariants

- `pdf/engine.js` owns the versioned engine and per-document session. Reader and
  cover use the same loader. Local Blobs use PDFDataRangeTransport + Blob.slice,
  256 KiB initial/chunk reads, at most two outstanding reads, no speculative
  full-file fetch. PDF structure may still require reading most/all bytes.
- Render with `page.render({ canvas, ... })`, never a supplied canvasContext:
  the latter opts out of PDF.js renderer workers. Preserve a readable old canvas
  while a staging canvas renders; record actual isWorkerRendering after finish.
  Unsupported environments retain PDF.js cooperative main-thread fallback.
- Foreground jobs precede prefetch. Cancel obsolete nonvisible draws. Neighbour
  previews that become visible while running must subsequently refine to HiDPI.
  Translation text prefetch waits for readable/idle rendering; cover aborts when
  leaving the library. Closing/replacing a document destroys both worker roles.
- Full canvases respect 10M pixel / 8192 dimension limits; neighbour previews
  additionally cap at 2M pixels. Snapshot LRU accounts estimated width*height*4
  bytes, caps at 48 MiB, closes evicted ImageBitmaps, and clears per document.
  This is a snapshot budget, not a total browser/PDF decoder memory guarantee.
- Continuous layout uses a prefix-height index and two spacers, with bounded
  nearby rows (7 at normal scale, up to 33 when zoomed out). Do not create or
  measure one DOM placeholder for every page. Geometry restores anchors in the
  same layout commit; explicit page navigation is atomic. A late restore cannot
  override subsequent user navigation. Paged mode always owns an explicit page.
- `test:pdf-browser` checks real renderer use, sparse range reads, bounds and
  whole-page/fit-width anchoring. `test:pdf-performance` covers vectors/scans,
  mixed sizes, cache latency and worker teardown; `--hidpi` checks refinement.
